newsitem.title: USA: US stocks tumble on dollar, blue chip profit woes.
newsitem.headline: US stocks tumble on dollar, blue chip profit woes.

text.p: A calmer Wall Street traded sideways midday, catching its breath after falling headlong once again in one of the most volatile weeks for some time.
Analysts pinned the blame for the latest rout on the ailing dollar, weaker bonds and fears over blue chip earnings.
"Right now we are just hanging sideways, licking our wounds," said Doug Myers, vice-president of equity trading at Interstate/Johnson Lane.
Midday, the Dow was down 73.63 points or 0.93 percent to 7868.40, well off the day's low of 7818.46.
Double-witching stocks and index options expirations fueled the early volatility, analysts said.

News that Gillette Co said it guided analysts' earnings estimates lower Thursday night rattled sentiment, provoking a deja-vu fear over blue chip earnings following last Friday's reports that Coca-Cola Co's profits may be less healthy than expected.
Gillette's stock tumbled to a low of 85-3/8 before easing slightly by midday when it traded at 86, off 4-3/16.
The New York Stock Exchange imposed trading curbs.
After the S&P 500 futures fell 12 points, sidecar curbs were imposed. Midday futures were off 10.30 points at 917.50.
The dollar slid against the German mark as currency players said they were adjusting to a possibly tighter Bundesbank monetary policy.

But preliminary figures from the University of Michigan, released midmorning Friday, showed consumer sentiment in August falling to 102.8 points against 107.1 final figure for July, easing fears over inflation.
The data helped to calm the dollar, bonds and stocks.
Shares in Pep Boys tumbled after Merrill Lynch cut the stock. Pep was down 7 at 26-1/16.
Most active on NYSE was SL Green Realty, making its initial public offering debut. The stock was up 4-1/4 at 25-1/4.
On NYSE, declines totaled 2174 compared with advances of 1538.
Nasdaq was down 10.76 at 1575.93 points. The long bond was off 13/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
